place.formattedAddress: Department of Museum, Jln Damansara, Tasik Perdana, 50566 Kuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

reviews.author: farid omar
reviews.text:
For history lover this is the must place to visit in Kuala Lumpur.
You can use public transportation to came here and it's very easy because the MRT station.
Entrance for Malaysian also very cheap.
Just enjoy your day and explore this museum slowly.
They also have some interactive game and information.
The toilet, cafe and  surau also is available inside this area so don't rush your time.
Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Amin Demanis
reviews.text:
National Museum of Malaysia is one of those places that you may not visit often, but when you do, it gives you a deeper sense of context about the country. It sits just outside the main city flow, but it is actually quite accessible. You can even take the MRT directly from Agile Residence and reach here without much effort.

I tend to spend more time on the traditional crafts section. The intricacy of songket, limar, and other fabrics really stands out when you see them up close. The Malay woodwork also caught my attention, there is a certain flow and harmony in the design. It is one of those skills I wish I had, purely for its artistic value. It makes you appreciate how much thought goes into these details.

Another part that went beyond my expectation was learning about the Orang Asli communities. The way their lifestyle and connection to nature are presented adds a different perspective, something you do not usually come across in everyday city life.

If you take your time, you can easily spend a whole day here just immersing in the history and exhibits. At the same time, I do feel there is room for better curation in some sections, where the storytelling could be made more engaging and easier to follow.

👉 If you’re exploring Kuala Lumpur as a place to live or invest, I share deeper KL living insights on my YouTube channel.

reviews.author: Shirlyn Green
reviews.text:
I spent a day at National Museum of Malaysia, and it was a very enjoyable and meaningful experience.

The ticket price is very cheap, making it absolutely worth a visit for both locals and tourists. It offers great value for money considering how much you can learn and explore inside.

I really love visiting the museum because I enjoy seeing historical items and learning the stories behind them. The exhibits give a good insight into Malaysia’s history and culture, and it was interesting to see many old artifacts up close.

Overall, it was a great experience, and I truly enjoyed spending time there. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who is interested in history or cultural exploration.

reviews.author: Shaista Rashid
reviews.text: I enjoyed visiting the National Museum of Malaysia. It is a great place to learn about the country’s history, culture, and traditions. The museum has interesting exhibits, beautiful displays, and a traditional Malaysian-style building. It was an educational and enjoyable experience, and I would recommend it to anyone who wants to understand Malaysia better.

reviews.author: Janson Yap
reviews.text: Nice musuem to learn about the history of Malaysia from prehistoric to ancient civilization to colonial to modern time. Entrance fee is relatively cheap (~$1.50) for non-citizen adults. Only thing I didn't like was the crowd and many kids jumping around the exhibitions but I guess that comes with the cheap fee. Spent 1.5hours here

reviews.author: Subhani Taha
reviews.text:
Batu Caves was one of the highlights of my trip to Malaysia. The place is absolutely stunning, from the giant golden statue at the entrance to the colorful staircase leading up to the caves. The atmosphere is unique, blending natural beauty, history, and culture all in one location. The climb can be a bit challenging, especially on a hot day, but the views and experience at the top make it completely worth it.

A couple of things visitors should know before going. Parking is not free, so make sure to bring some cash or be prepared to pay for parking. Also, keep an eye on your belongings because there are plenty of monkeys around. They are fun to watch and photograph, but they can be quite bold and may try to grab food, drinks, or anything they think looks interesting. As long as you’re careful, they’re part of what makes the experience memorable.

Overall, I had a great time visiting Batu Caves and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Kuala Lumpur. It’s a beautiful and iconic destination that offers much more than just great photo opportunities. Definitely worth a visit and an easy 5-star experience.

reviews.author: Itziar Azua
reviews.text: Totally worth it, not only for the temples and all the history behind the caves and the Tamil but the caves! This natural formation is breathtaking. Climbing the stairs early in the morning (7:30 am) was incredible as there were no crowds, the tour buses get there around 9:30 am so it is good going early. The monkeys were very fun to watch. Very aware that this is a worshipping place so it is important to be respectful, there are a lot of worshipers not there for tourism.

reviews.author: Mary M
reviews.text:
Be aware of the scam, it is free to visit but there will be people asking you to pay for parking or to go up. Just ignore them.

Getting here can be confusing, gps may take you another way which was incorrect so watch out for the signs.

Although, this is highly visited tourist area, this is very much a place of worship. At the time we attended it was mostly worshippers.

There is vast difference between going during the day vs night. It was less busy, we did not encounter any monkeys at night. We were able to take our time going up. There was nice breeze in the air.

Once you get up, there are more stairs to climb if you want to see another temple. The cave formations were unique to look at. There is a pungent smell in the air, it can be overpowering and make the experience a little enjoyable.

I do recommend bringing water to drink as it’s a steep climb/ descend.

reviews.author: VASU TAYAL
reviews.text:
Visited this place in Malaysia, truly it is one of the most iconic and breathtaking place. The massive golden statues of Lord Murugan at the entrances of the temple is absolutely stunning and good for photography.
Seeing this statue so close is an unforgettable experience.
There were so many colourful stairs, I climbed a little bit beacuse batu caves was in my package and after we have to visit another place but the view from that was beautiful.
There were plenty of monkeys around. It was hot at thay time so recommend to visit early in the morning.
Overall Batu Caves is a must visit when in Kuala Lumpur.

reviews.author: Dan Pieloch
reviews.text:
The Batu Caves were initially listed as a place of worship in 1890. The main daily draw is a massive 43m/141ft tall statue of Lord Murugan, which you can see without having to climb any of the 272 steps.

But, this is also where devotees come for the festival of Thaipusam, celebrated on the full moon day in the Tamil month of Thai on the confluence of star Pusam. I could not find different details as to the dates than this.

There are several temples on the ground floor outside, and inside the cave as well. We did not enter any of the temples because we did not want to remove our shoes. People and monkeys and pigeons are all over this entire property, and they've all made a mess that doesn't appear to get addressed by the staff. Also, lots of folks walk everywhere with no shoes on, and then walk into the temples with those same no-shoe feet. No thank you. However, this is still an interesting place to visit, and worth a trip out here if you're in Kuala Lumpur. Free to enter the main areas, but there's a small fee to enter one of the caves. Still worth it.

place.formattedAddress: Kemensah Heights, 68000 Ampang Jaya, Selangor, Malaysia

reviews.author: Tehseen Khan
reviews.text:
Zoo Negara is a fantastic place for a family day out and offers hours of fun for both kids and adults. The zoo is spacious, clean, and home to a wide variety of animals from around the world.

One of the biggest highlights of the visit was seeing the famous giant pandas.
Even though they were peacefully sleeping, it was still an adorable and memorable experience. Watching them relax in their specially designed habitat was a reminder of just how calm and lovable these amazing animals are.

The zoo is well maintained, with shaded walkways, clear signs, and plenty of opportunities to learn about wildlife conservation.
There are many different animal exhibits to explore, making every section interesting and enjoyable. The staff are friendly, and the overall atmosphere is relaxing and family-friendly.

Plan to spend at least half a day here to enjoy everything at a comfortable pace. Bring comfortable walking shoes, stay hydrated, and don't forget your camera there are plenty of wonderful photo opportunities throughout the zoo. Whether you're an animal lover or simply looking for a fun outing, Zoo Negara is definitely worth visiting, and meeting the adorable pandas is an experience you'll remember long after your trip.

reviews.author: Hazmin Freecs
reviews.text:
Visited on a Monday with my mother and sister. Overall, we had a great experience and managed to see almost every animal we were interested in. The tiger was definitely one of the highlights of the trip.
The zoo was cleaner and more active than I expected for a weekday, and the animal show was surprisingly crowded. We arrived before 11 AM and most of the seating area was already full. I would recommend arriving at the zoo before 9 AM if you want a more relaxed visit and better chances of getting good seats for the show.
One thing to note is that several areas were under renovation during our visit. Unfortunately, the elephants, lions and cheetahs were not available, which was a little disappointing as these are some of the animals many visitors look forward to seeing.
I would also like to suggest an improvement regarding the souvenir photo service. The photographers did a very good job and the photos looked great, but the pricing felt too high for most visitors. The cheapest option available during our visit was a framed photo at around RM60, which many families may find difficult to justify. I believe offering digital copies (softcopy) at RM20–RM30 each would encourage more visitors to purchase their photos. Many people today prefer keeping memories on their phones, and I think more affordable digital options could increase sales while making visitors happier. The photos were genuinely well taken, and I would have considered purchasing a few of them if a more affordable softcopy option had been available.
Despite the renovations, we still enjoyed the visit and managed to cover almost the entire zoo. A good family outing and worth visiting again once the renovation work is completed.

reviews.author: Red Plus TV
reviews.text:
Our visit to Zoo Negara Malaysia was absolutely amazing! The entire place is beautifully landscaped, clean, and very spacious, making it incredibly easy and enjoyable to walk around with the family.

The highlight of our day was definitely the animals, especially the majestic tigers and the adorable giant pandas, who all looked healthy and well-cared for. We also spent time at the animal show amphitheater, which was fantastic! The presentation was entertaining, highly educational, and perfect for visitors of all ages. The zoo's facilities are excellent too, featuring plenty of shaded areas, clean restrooms, and great spots to grab refreshments.

What truly made our trip unforgettable, though, was the world-class hospitality. We want to give a special shoutout to a staff Zoo Camp member named Khairun. Khairun was incredibly friendly, kind, and went completely out of their way to make us feel welcome with a warm smile. Wonderful facilities, beautiful wildlife, and amazing staff like Khairun make Zoo Negara a must-visit destination. We highly recommend it and will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Aqilah Zulkarnain
reviews.text:
First zoo negara visit and..it wasnt bad but I wish it could be better 🥺

First off, it is definitely a nice way to spend time with your loved ones here, but do remember to bring a fan and umbrella as it can get pretty hot and humid. Though there are some shaded areas and plenty of seated gazebo areas too, its mostly hot everywhere else in the park..

As for the animals, there were so many to see but somehow.. was kind of expecting the animal exhibits to be more…well kept I guess? Construction was going on in a few places so I guess thats a good sign.

Apart from that, you wont be thirsty or hungry, since there are several eateries across the park (albeit a bit expensive 😅)

All in all..a good place to spend your time (and money) but deep down im wishing they renovated the place a lot lot more..idk thats just me tho.

Quick summary;
Parking: RM15 per entry (if you park inside) and RM16 per parking spot outside.
Entrance is free throughout your birthday month but it has to be on your birthday OR 30 days from your birth date
Kids less than 3 get free entry!
Once you enter the park you’ll be ushered to take family pictures with the professional photographers. We bought the framed photos for rm180 and got 6 + 6 fridge magnets as well :)
Food = kinda a scam but as expected, rm16 for 9 nuggets.. 🫣

reviews.author: Riyas Jamaluddin (Docree)
reviews.text: We were there today and it was hot if you are with kids take lots of water and shade and be prepared to sweat. We took the ride inside to the tiger area. Many of the animals were asleep as it was hot. Saw the panda for the first time. It was an amazing experience. Many area of the zoo were under maintenance. I liked it but it was tiring. Umbrella would be a good idea. Bathrooms are pretty neat and clean. There is a mosque inside so you can pray. The Aquatic animal shape is entertaining for the kids. Overall it’s a good place to spend a day with the kids.
